[Thinking]
**Summarizing a playful lesson**

The user is asking about "If You Give a Mouse a Cookie," likely wanting a fun explanation of the escalating requests that come from giving the mouse a cookie. In the story, this simple act leads to a chain reaction of demands. The moral is clear: small favors can lead to larger commitments, so it's important to set boundaries. I could also mention that feeding real mice can attract pests, but that might not be their intent!
[/Thinking]

It’s a playful nod to the book “If You Give a Mouse a Cookie.” In the story, giving a mouse a cookie triggers a chain of ever-growing requests—milk, a straw, a napkin, a mirror, a haircut, a broom, a nap, a story—until he ends up wanting another cookie. The joke (and gentle lesson) is that small favors can snowball into a lot more than you planned, so it’s wise to set boundaries and anticipate follow-on asks.

Literally speaking, feeding a real mouse is also a bad idea—it encourages pests to stick around and can lead to infestations.
